inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares Q2 2026 10-Q (361.3m; H1-2026 362.2m). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting as well would double-count.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL companyfacts FY2025 10-K: ShareBasedCompensation 94.8 + PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation 33.9 (no combined adjusted-EBITDA figure published, so the two lines are summed).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.2% (US 10y), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.6 (CME's measured beta is ~0.3-0.5; floored at 0.6 for regulatory/structural risk) -> CoE ~7.2%; debt is ~3% of market cap at ~4.5% pre-tax, so WACC ~7.2%. 7.5% used in every scenario; risk is charged through the scenarios and weights, not by per-scenario WACC.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (Chicago HQ, data centres) are small relative to flows and sit inside operating expense/OI as reported under ASC 842; lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt (one treatment: in the flows).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF. CME is an operating company (exchange + clearinghouse), not a bank: clearing-member performance bonds and guaranty-fund cash are member collateral, not CME funding, and are excluded from both cash and debt. Routing row: operating company. NON-OPERATING OPERATING STREAMS folded into ebitda_margin_path (revenue stays = reported operating revenue so the growth path is interpretable): (1) net earnings on reinvested cash collateral -- FY2025 InvestmentIncomeNonoperating 5,736.5 less OtherNonoperatingIncomeExpense -4,833.8 (mostly interest paid back to clearing firms) less the one-off 352.8 Q4-2025 gain on investments = ~550 recurring; TTM to Jun-26 ~645; less ~105 estimated interest on CME's own corporate cash (stripped because that cash sits in the net-debt bridge) -> ~540 collateral spread, ~7.7% of FY2026 revenue, projected flat-to-down in dollars as the Fed eases; (2) equity-method earnings, mainly the 27% S&P Dow Jones Indices stake, FY2025 371.7 (H1-26 200.1), ~5.7% of revenue, grown with revenue. The stake is therefore valued in the flows and NOT added again in the equity bridge. AMORTIZATION: FY2025 D&A tag 107.5 is depreciation only; amortization of acquired intangibles (223.4, CBOT/NYMEX/NEX, largely stock deals and not tax-deductible) is added back in EBITDA but EXCLUDED from da_pct_path, so it gets no perpetual tax shield. da_pct_path = depreciation only. FY0 operating adj EBITDA ex-SBC = OI 4,229.5 + dep 107.5 + amort 223.4 + SBC 94.8 = 4,655.2 (71.4%); +collateral ~7.9% +JV ~5.7% ~= 85% all-in. Unlevered: interest expense (173.4) not in flows; debt in net debt. Year-1 (FY2026) anchored to H1-2026 revenue 3,586.3 (+7.6% YoY), July-26 ADV tracking +18%, adj opex guide ~$1.695bn ex-license fees, capex ~$85m, tax rate low end of 23.5-24.5%. last_fcf = 4,193.6 - 128.7 - 105 (estimated corporate-cash interest). BUYBACKS: XBRL shows no share repurchase outflows since before FY2022 (the Analysis JSON's '$695M buybacks' in Q2 2026 is not corroborated by the cash-flow tags); CME returns capital through regular + annual variable dividends (FY2025 dividends paid 3,933.0). The flat count is therefore a modelling convention the company funds only partially -- diluted shares drifted 358.5m (FY20) -> 361.3m (Q2-26), ~0.15%/yr, consistent with SBC being the only dilution. Net debt uses Jun-26 cash (post the January variable dividend), excluding the 131.4 marketable securities (deferred-comp assets offset by liabilities).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (1.7% 5yr) diverges far more than 30% from revenue (6.0%) and EPS (13.7%) CAGRs. Book value is meaningless as a growth proxy here: CME pays out ~100% of earnings via regular + annual variable dividends, so equity is flat by policy. Revenue 5yr CAGR is used instead; EPS CAGR is inflated by rate-driven collateral income (FY2020 near-zero rates -> FY2023-25 ~5%) and the FY2025 352.8 investment gain.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes (corporate-cash interest not stripped historically; not separately disclosed per year). Owner-FCF CAGR is slightly ABOVE reported, so SBC is not outgrowing cash flow (SBC ~1.5-2% of revenue). Much of FY2022-25 FCF growth came from the rate cycle lifting collateral income from ~zero, which is not repeatable.

base.margin_note: Operating adj EBITDA ex-SBC ~72.3% FY26 rising to ~73.5% (expense discipline, operating leverage) + collateral spread 7.7% of revenue FY26 fading to ~5.4% as rates ease with balances growing + S&P DJI JV ~5.7% held flat as a share of revenue.
base.narrative: Volumes normalise off record FY2025-26 levels but secular hedging demand, market data (+20%) and new products (24/7 crypto, event contracts) keep revenue compounding ~5%; rates drift down so collateral income shrinks in dollars early.

bull.narrative: Rates stay 'higher for longer' and volatile: rate-futures volume and collateral balances both stay elevated; crypto/event contracts and tokenised collateral become real revenue lines; operating leverage lifts operating margin toward 75%.

bear.narrative: A Fed cutting cycle roughly halves the collateral spread and calms rate volatility, so FY2027 volumes fall back from record highs; Cboe/ICE take share in equity-index and energy, prediction markets grow outside CME, and rate-per-contract erodes -- growth ~3% and all-in margin compresses ~5pp.

scenario_narratives.base: CME's benchmark rate (SOFR/Treasury) and equity-index futures franchise keeps its liquidity network effect; FY2026 revenue lands ~+7.5% (H1 +7.6%, July ADV +18%), then growth fades to ~5% as volumes normalise off records, with market data and new products (24/7 crypto, event contracts, FTSE Russell licence secured to 2037) offsetting modest rate-per-contract erosion. The Fed eases gradually, so the collateral spread (~$540m) shrinks in dollars and from ~7.7% to ~5.4% of revenue; operating margin creeps up on the ~$1.7bn expense guide. The Duffy->Fitzpatrick handover (Mar-2027) is internal and uneventful.
scenario_narratives.bull: Rates stay high and volatile and fiscal/term-premium uncertainty keeps rate futures and Treasury hedging at record volumes; cleared-collateral balances keep growing so the collateral spread holds its dollars; crypto 24/7, event contracts and Google Cloud tokenised collateral scale into meaningful lines, and market data keeps compounding double digits. Revenue grows 7-9% early, operating margin approaches 75%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Volume is cyclical to rate and macro volatility: a Fed cutting cycle both compresses rate-futures activity and roughly halves the collateral spread. Competition bites at the margin -- Cboe's FTSE Russell options licence, ICE's MSCI/FTSE futures push, and Kalshi/Polymarket/DraftKings capturing event-contract volume outside CME -- while volume tiers erode rate per contract. FY2027 revenue is roughly flat after a strong FY2026 and long-run growth settles ~3%, all-in margin down ~5pp, and a lower exit multiple as the market re-rates CME as ex-growth.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (up from 15%): FY2025-26 volumes and collateral income are at or near records, so the base year is closer to a peak than a trough and the Fed path is two-sided. Base 55%: the franchise is a regulated quasi-monopoly in its core products and the base needs no heroics. Bull 25% (down from 35%): it needs high rates, record volumes and new-product traction to persist together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: CME is valued as a capital-light operating franchise on owner FCF, with the rate-sensitive collateral spread and the S&P DJI stake carried inside the flows rather than as separate balance-sheet assets, and amortization of acquired intangibles given no perpetual tax shield. At a 7.5% WACC the terminal cap binds in base and bull, so the value is largely a function of the exit multiple assumed on a ~3% grower.
key_risks_to_valuation: Collateral-income sensitivity to the Fed path: ~7-8% of revenue-equivalent that could halve in a cutting cycle
Volume normalisation from record FY2025-26 levels (base year may be near a cyclical peak)
Competitive encroachment in equity index (Cboe, ICE) and event contracts (Kalshi, Polymarket)
Terminal value dominance: the 20x cap on a ~3% terminal growth binds; a lower exit multiple moves value roughly one-for-one
